finalText:
React re-renders every child by default whenever the parent re-renders, no matter if the props changed. Same props doesn't stop it — you have to opt out.

Two fixes work together:

1. Wrap the child in `React.memo`. This tells React to skip re-rendering if the props are the same as last time.
2. Make sure the props are actually the same, not just equal in value. If you pass an inline function or object like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}`, React sees a brand new function or object every render — even though it looks the same to you. Wrap those in `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent so the reference stays stable.

If you skip step 2, `React.memo` alone won't help, since it checks by reference, not by deep value.

One more thing worth knowing: `React.memo` only checks props. If the child reads from context, and that context value changes, it'll still re-render even when memoized.
